claims.text: Start by searching a people-search site for your name or other identifying information such as a phone number or address.
When you find a report about yourself, locate the site's opt-out or removal instructions and follow them.
Repeat the opt-out process across other relevant people-search sites; doing this one by one can be time-consuming.
Periodically recheck people-search sites and submit new opt-out requests if your information reappears.
Opting out of people-search sites does not delete information from public records, so the workflow reduces exposure rather than guaranteeing total deletion.
Consumers can perform people-search opt-outs themselves for free or pay a service to perform the work on their behalf.
